accuracy.reason: All eight card objectives have accurate bounded claims; diagrams distinguish hit/miss and source versus stale copy without promising synchronization.

evidence.quote: Invalidation alone does not guarantee freshness.

mechanisms.reason: Cards 1-7 identify copy creation, application reads/fills, key inputs, old-fill race, removal causes, copy scope and bounded source work; learner transfers each mechanism.

evidence.quote: A reader can fetch $20 before the update, pause, then refill $20 after removal. The next cache hit still returns $20.

coherence.reason: Reuse leads to paths and ownership, then mutable copies, removal, topology, failure load and choice. Prerequisites precede the decisions they enable.

evidence.quote: A hit can still return outdated data. Presence in a cache does not prove that the value matches its source.

decisions.reason: Card 8 combines expense, reuse, freshness and measured capacity; cards 6-7 add network/availability tradeoffs and actionable bounded fallback.

evidence.quote: If requests rarely reuse results, or freshness is too hard to maintain, the cache may cost more than it saves.

clarity.reason: Terms are defined with actors and effects; currency and old-price examples clarify correctness. No recurring story is needed for the connected progression.

evidence.quote: An entry can be evicted before its TTL ends.

outcomes.reason: Learner covers all five criteria: reuse savings, station/language key, hit without source, application miss/fill/return and database plus lookup/write cost. Cards 1-3 support each.
Card 4 directly teaches old fill after deletion, old response and lack of freshness guarantee; card 8 source-authority decision supports bypass. Learner transfers the race correctly.
Card 5 supports both request timelines, early capacity removal, lifetime not freshness/residency and no automatic replacement; learner applies all correctly.
Card 6 supports old local copies, shared choice, lookup locations, network/operations cost and local versus common cache-access loss without implying sync or total application failure.
Card 7 teaches duplicate concurrent reads, shared in-progress lookup and capped/error outage fallback. Learner uses safe capacity and rejects assuming stale data exists outside failed cache.
Cards 1 and 8 support no-cache decision, no later reuse, adequate latency/capacity, added operations/storage and reconsideration based on substantial repeated source work with acceptable freshness.

sourceChecks.claim: Microsoft supports reuse benefits, initial fill/lookup costs, authority and selective adoption; key dimensions prevent mixing distinct answers.
Microsoft application miss/read/fill sequence agrees with slide and hit/miss diagram.

Microsoft warns cache-aside does not guarantee consistency; explicit read-before-write/fill-after-delete sequence demonstrates why invalidation alone fails. Source-authority fallback is valid under contract assumptions.
Redis eviction and noeviction policies support capacity removal before TTL; AWS expiration section corroborates distinct time lifetime and later refill.
AWS local/external sections support independent versions, network/shared service costs and cache-access failure scope.
AWS coalescing and capped fallback/load shedding support both protection mechanisms; old data is conditional, not promised available from a failed cache.
